analysis.title: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA): 3Q Preview: Expect strong results/guidance, with focus on power/shell and customer funding needs through 2028
key_insights: GS expects three debates to dominate the print: management visibility into datacenter power/shell capacity through 2028, sustainability of AI infrastructure funding, and broader AI demand health (agentic-driven CPU upside, customer ROI, enterprise adoption).

GS sees a favorable setup after the recent sector-wide selloff and expects near-term fundamentals to outpace Street estimates. It reiterates Buy with the stock at about 11X its CY27 EPS estimate of $16.70.
GS acknowledges near-term challenges for the stock until investors get more visibility into the power/shell and funding debates.
GS expects solid 3Q results and 4Q guidance above the Street, driven by better-than-expected margins. Its 3Q and 4Q EPS estimates are both 6% above the Street.

GS sees limited execution risk for 2027 datacenter deployments. Power/shell availability in 2028 is the focus, and disclosure on customer readiness or 2028 revenue tied to buildouts already under construction could help size forecast risk.
GS expects more scrutiny of AI infrastructure funding in a higher-rate environment, particularly for emerging hyperscalers and neoclouds that rely on external capital.
GS expects focus on Nvidia's datacenter CPU opportunity as agentic AI lifts CPU demand. CPU-only racks are expected to ship in 2H26.

With input costs elevated, particularly HBM, gross margin sustainability through 2028 is a key focus. Longer term, investors will watch margin preservation as competition intensifies and customers prioritize lower token costs and stronger returns.
GS expects focus on Nvidia's longer-term competitive position as AMD's MI450X Helios rack-scale systems gain traction with more AI model builders and hyperscalers continue custom ASIC ramps.
GS expects post-print focus on power and shell availability in 2027/28, funding datapoints for emerging hyperscalers and neoclouds, and hyperscaler monetization and ROI trends.

market_movers.rationale: 12-month price target of $300 is based on a 30X P/E applied to normalized EPS of $10.00. Price was $186.64 at the 6 Nov 2026 close, implying 60.7% upside.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees a favorable setup for Nvidia after the sector-wide selloff, with near-term fundamentals expected to beat the Street.

earnings_insights: FY3Q27E (GS estimate, not yet reported): revenue $110,081mn vs Street $109,282mn (+1%), gross margin incl. SBC 74.1% vs Street 73.1%, operating income incl. SBC $74,216mn vs Street $70,344mn (+6%), operating margin 67.4% vs 64.4%, EPS incl. SBC $2.57 vs Street $2.42 (+6%).

FY4Q27E (GS estimate, Street is Visible Alpha consensus): revenue $124,814mn vs Street $124,290mn (0%), gross margin incl. SBC 72.2% vs 71.5%, operating income $81,993mn vs $78,660mn (+4%), operating margin 65.7% vs 63.3%, EPS incl. SBC $2.88 vs $2.73 (+6%).

FY3Q27E segments (GS est vs Street): Datacenter $102,551mn vs $101,790mn (+1%), Edge Computing $7,530mn vs $7,492mn (+1%). FY4Q27E: Datacenter $116,908mn vs $116,945mn (0%), Edge Computing $7,906mn vs $7,345mn (+8%).

FY2027E (GS est vs Street): revenue $412,731mn vs $411,164mn, EPS incl. SBC $9.40 vs $9.33 (+1%), gross margin 74.0% vs 73.8%. FY2028E: revenue $718,299mn vs $699,242mn (+3%), EPS $16.70 vs $15.94 (+5%), gross margin 72.8% vs 73.0%. FY2029E: revenue $954,992mn vs $914,218mn (+4%), EPS $23.00 vs $20.96 (+10%), gross margin 73.0% vs 74.2%.

GS forecasts by fiscal year ending January: revenue $215,938mn in FY1/26 (actual), $412,731mn in 1/27E, $718,300mn in 1/28E, $954,992mn in 1/29E. EPS $4.52 in 1/26, then $9.40, $16.70 and $23.00 estimated. P/E 35.0X, 19.9X, 11.2X and 8.1X.

vol_and_positioning: GS believes positioning is favorable going into the print after the recent selloff, which raised investor concerns about power and shell capacity constraints on 2028 datacenter expansion.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects solid 3Q results and 4Q guidance above the Street on better margins, limited 2027 execution risk, and favorable positioning after the selloff, with the stock at about 11X CY27 EPS of $16.70.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors worry about datacenter power and shell capacity for 2028, funding for emerging hyperscalers and neoclouds in a higher-rate environment, elevated HBM input costs and rising competition from AMD and custom ASICs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management gives no clear visibility on 2028 power/shell capacity or customer readiness, or funding datapoints for emerging hyperscalers and neoclouds deteriorate.

theme_stances.key_argument: Limited execution risk in 2027, and better disclosure on 2028 buildouts could alleviate investor concerns.
